# 01 — Merge plan: open-instinct × openinstinct

> Captured 2026-10-29. Historical reasoning; the authoritative package layout now lives in
> ARCHITECTURE.md (channels became a plugin system; hosting became one self-hosted daemon on a
> VPS, remote server, home hardware, or laptop, ADR-015 and ADR-017; persona and curiosity were
> added). The 7-tier matrix, peers, payments, and voice below are deferred (ADR-020).

Short version: the two projects are complementary rather than overlapping.
**open-instinct** is strong on *who may do what* (multi-principal trust, grants, payments,
voice, cloud hosting) and weak on memory. **openinstinct** is strong on *how the agent
runs* (session semantics, memory engine, background work, exact-approval gate, durable
delivery) and deliberately narrow (one owner, one Mac, no voice, no groups). The right
merge is: openinstinct's runtime core wrapped in open-instinct's policy/network/hosting
shell.

## 1. Non-negotiables before writing code

| Issue | Detail | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| **License mismatch** | open-instinct is MIT. openinstinct's `main` branch has no LICENSE file; its README only says "source under this repository's license" and that its memory engine is copied from gajae-way at a pinned commit. | Treat openinstinct as **spec, not source**. Re-implement its designs from `docs/architecture.md`; don't vendor its code. Ask the author for a license or check gajae-way's. |
| **Different runtimes** | open-instinct: Node 22 / pnpm monorepo, Pi agent loop, any Pi provider. openinstinct: Bun daemon + Swift panel, one persistent `gjc` SDK session. | Pick one loop. Pi is the pragmatic choice (provider-agnostic, already in an MIT codebase); port openinstinct's *session semantics* onto it. |
| **Different trust models** | open-instinct resolves a principal and tier for every sender. openinstinct never promotes a non-owner message to an owner turn; peers are admitted only as `third_party` observations. | Keep both: open-instinct's tier table for *capability*, openinstinct's "owner authority minted only in ingress" rule for *authority*. |

## 2. What to take from each

### From open-instinct (the shell)

| Component | Why it's the better version |
|---|---|
| **Capability-tagged tools + 7-tier matrix** | Each tool is tagged with capabilities; `beforeToolCall` checks tier defaults, then grants, then spend/scope limits, logs to `audit.jsonl` |
| **Plain-English grants** | Model emits `trust_grant {to, capabilities, scope{purpose, window, maxUsd}, expiresAt, note}`; additive, never above owner, auto-expire |
| **Principal hardening** | Owner recognised only on carrier-bound channels; email from the owner's own address drops to a `partner`-tier `owner:email` principal because `From` can be forged |
| **Group-thread isolation** | Each participant gets their own transcript; owner's turns run at the lowest tier present; a bare "yes" in a group never settles an approval |
| **"Enforced twice"** | Requester gets a polite no; owner gets a one-line notice (rate-limited 1/conversation/hour) and an audit entry |
| **Approval UX** | Short token ("yes K7P2"), strict bare-yes rules, approval bound to tool+args hash+amount within 5%, valid 15 min |
| **Payments** | Stripe Link one-time cards; owner sees exact amount + merchant before a card exists; blocked-merchant list applies to every tier |
| **Voice + hosted identity** | Inkbox gives number/email/A2A endpoint; Voice AI dials and reports by text |
| **Per-user microVM + gateway** | Maritime VM with Linux desktop; gateway provisions one agent per signup |
| **Desktop takeover for logins/2FA** | Logins, 2FA and payments go to the human via takeover or Link, never to the model alone |

### From openinstinct (the core)

| Component | Why it's the better version |
|---|---|
| **Persistent main session** | One session reopened over the same transcript across restarts, never respawned per message; serial queue; steering (`interruptMode=wait`, `steeringMode=all`); segment flushing at each tool-call start so the owner gets several short texts; inactivity watchdog; daemon-managed compaction at ≥50% |
| **`OwnerTurnIngress`** | One source-agnostic entry point for every channel: echo, pause suppression, steer-when-busy, failure breaker, memory capture, segment handling |
| **gajae-way memory** | Git-backed Markdown axes; append-only `daily/` capture; 6-hourly canonicalization into `people/projects/decisions`; daily structural audit; BM25 recall; `MEMORY.md` is a generated map, not a store |
| **Children + receipts** | Separate in-process sessions (cap 4 concurrent / 16 live), lifecycle `running → idle → cold → terminated`, terminal reports become receipts folded into the main session as triage turns; **only the main session may message the owner** |
| **Monitors** | `cron` / `watcher` / `webhook` / `script` triggers; replay-safe propagation `admitted → batched → dispatched → authored → delivered`; errors never reach the owner raw |
| **Managed tool gate** | Every proposal = action ID + revision + SHA-256 digest; `effect_started` persisted before invocation; unverifiable results settle `ambiguous`, never retried blindly |
| **Managed HTTP** | `secretRef` bindings resolved only on exact origin+header; no redirects; DNS pinned; cloud-metadata blocked; prompt content can't edit host policy |
| **Durable outbox** | Idempotency keys, bounded retry ladder, `confirmed / expired / failed_ambiguous` |
| **Browser pinning** | Tool calls blocked unless pinned to the agent's own Chrome profile |
| **Peer envelope** | Single-line `OI-PEER/1` JSON with single-use nonce; malformed → `undefined`; trust re-checked at send time so revocation stops already-approved sends |

## 3. Where they conflict — and how to resolve

| Conflict | open-instinct | openinstinct | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Memory** | Single `MEMORY.md` with a `## Preferences` section that tiers see partial cuts of | Full axis tree with canonicalization/audit | Use gajae-way layout. Map open-instinct's tier visibility onto **axes**, not headings: `partner` → `people/` + preferences, `friend` → free/busy only, etc. The `memory.write` capability stays owner-only. |
| **Approvals** | Friendly short token, fuzzy natural-language settle via `approval_settle` | Exact `/approve ID REV DIGEST`; conversation text is never approval | **Both layers.** Externally keep the short token and bare-yes rules; internally the token *is* a lookup to the exact (id, revision, digest) triple, and settlement writes `effect_started` before execution. Keep open-instinct's rule that money never settles via model inference. |
| **Who talks to the owner** | Tools like `notify_owner` can text from policy code | Only main-session triage turns are owner-facing | Route policy notices into the **notification ledger** (openinstinct's proactive-output path) rather than letting guard code send directly. Rate-limit and audit from open-instinct, delivery durability from openinstinct. |
| **Hosting** | Cloud microVM per person | Owner's own Mac, own Chrome profile | Make the **host an interface**. Local mode wins on CAPTCHAs/cookies/residential IP (the exact failure Instinct itself hits); cloud mode wins for multi-user and always-on. Ship both behind one `computer` package, like open-instinct's `packages/computer` already abstracts Maritime vs hosted MCP. |
| **Peers** | 7 tiers, grants, invitations, A2A over Inkbox | Binary allow-list, observation-only, no model tool can enroll peers | Tiers for *capability*; openinstinct's rule that **enrolment/revocation is a control-plane op, not a model tool** for *authority*. Inbound peer messages run in their own principal transcript (open-instinct) and never become owner turns (openinstinct). |
| **Channels** | Inkbox (hosted iMessage/SMS/email/voice) | `chat.db` reader + AppleScript sender, dedicated Apple ID | Channel adapter interface with both implementations; both feed `OwnerTurnIngress`. Carry openinstinct's cursor-fingerprint trick (anchor at `max(ROWID)`, replay nothing on identity change — it exists because an early build texted 21 failures to the owner). |

## 4. Proposed package layout (original; superseded by ARCHITECTURE.md)

~~~
packages/
  ingress/      OwnerTurnIngress + channel adapters (inkbox, imessage-local, chat-socket, email)
  session/      persistent main session on Pi: serial queue, steer, segments, watchdog, compaction, reload
  memory/       gajae-way-style engine: axes.json, daily capture, canonicalize (6h), audit (daily),
                debloat, BM25 search, MEMORY.md map, git closure ladder w/ mutation-id trailer
  policy/       capability tags, 7-tier matrix, grants, spend policy, principal resolution, audit.jsonl
  gate/         managed executor: action id/rev/digest, effect_started, ambiguous settlement,
                approval tokens ↔ digest triple, /allow-send rules
  children/     background sessions, lifecycle, receipts → triage
  monitors/     cron/watcher/webhook/script, propagation state machine
  delivery/     durable outbox, notification ledger, plaintext sanitizer
  computer/     host interface: local-mac (pinned Chrome) | maritime-vm | hosted-mcp
  http/         managed HTTP with secretRef bindings, DNS pinning
  network/      contacts, tiers, invitations, OI-PEER/1 envelope, trust re-check at send
  payments/     Stripe Link wallet + merchant policy
  voice/        Inkbox Voice AI (phone.call capability, ask-by-default)
  apps/         Composio tool router
  server/ gateway/ cli/
skills/         playbooks
~~~

Keep the gajae-way axis set as the default — `daily, events, tasks, people, projects,
channels, decisions, ops/{rules,distillations,handoffs}, reflections` — with each axis
defined by a descriptor (`root`, `layout`, `appendOnly`, `retrievalPriority`, `promotesTo`)
so audit/retrieval never special-case an axis by name. The `ops/rules` partition is where
open-instinct's prompt/persona files and skills playbooks belong.

## 5. Build order

1. **Session + ingress + delivery** on Pi, with the local `chat` socket channel only. Prove
   restart-over-transcript, steering, segment flushing, outbox.
2. **Memory** — implement the capture → canonicalize → audit loop and the closure ladder
   (intent in DB → write daily + regenerate map → commit with a mutation-id trailer →
   receipt; quarantine on unrecoverable evidence). Add the audit diagnostics
   (`map_dangling`, `orphan_file`, `axis_layout_violation`, `map_content_drift`, …) as a
   CI gate.
3. **Gate + policy** — capability tags on every tool, tier matrix, grants,
   approval-token→digest binding, audit.jsonl. Port open-instinct's smoke test: stranger's
   agent asks for the calendar over A2A → only `notify_owner` allowed → one owner text →
   nothing from memory leaves the process.
4. **Children + monitors** — seed `memory-canonicalize` and `memory-audit` as protected
   monitors, as openinstinct does. *(Extended: `curiosity` monitor, see PERSONA.md.)*
5. **Channels** — Inkbox first (multi-user), local iMessage second. *(Superseded: channels
   are now plugins; web → Telegram → WhatsApp → iMessage → Signal → email.)*
6. **Computer** — local pinned-Chrome mode, then Maritime. *(Superseded: local Chromium →
   Docker → Firecracker.)*
7. **Network, payments, voice** — last, because each adds a new way to commit the owner to
   something.

## 6. Things neither project solves (from the Instinct teardown)

Both still inherit Instinct's gaps: no procedural/skill memory, no multimodal memory, no
automatic forgetting, and weak implicit personalization. gajae-way's `reflections` →
`ops/rules` promotion path is the closest hook for procedural memory, and its `debloat`
job (split files over 100 KB into indexed directories) is at least a bloat control.
Explicit forgetting (dated corrections, retention policy per axis) and the owner profile
+ curiosity loop (PERSONA.md) are Jaari's own additions.
